sasha: heads-up: hit a short cold-start iops wall in ap-southeast1 around 02:07 UTC. lots of tinywrites + fsync stalls, GPU attach timeouts for warmup jobs. attach rate dipped ~40% for ~4m.

omar: which pool/cohort? any iostat/KMSG?

sasha: cohort ap-se1-poolC (ephemeral). iostat snippet from one host: ```iostat -x 1 2
Device: r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await  %util
nvme0n1 0.00 512.00 0.00 12544.00 49.00 9.50 18.2 0.1 18.1 99.8
```

chen: avgqu and util are saturated. did cleaner run overlap with cold starts?

sasha: yes — janitor schedule shows a batch of scrub jobs kicked at 02:05 UTC (controller accepted then hit rate-limit). janitor-bot: "enqueue scrub cohort=ap-se1-poolC id=8421" then "scheduler: rate-limit hit" events, followed by multiple hosts starting scrub at 02:06 when rate-limit lifted.

rachel: combo of scrub + coldstart attach spike = tinywrites avalanche. cold-start workloads generate many fsyncs while model artifacts extracted.

omar: immediate mitigations? my vote: 1) set scrub backoff 2) increase attach timeout to avoid fallback churn 3) temporarily divert coldstarts to warm pool or dedicated nodes if possible.

sasha: agreed. I'm going to issue a fast backoff and lower janitor concurrency for this pool. ops-bot: `scheduler set-backoff --pool ap-se1-poolC --duration 900s`

chen: also recommend adding a short pre-warm step so coldstarts write to RAMfs for initial extraction then flush later — longer-term but helpful.

omar: short-term attach timeout bump from 30s->120s in autoscaler should reduce fallback. also consider marking coldstart jobs as "deferred-attach" when pool IO>80%.

rachel: can we throttle snapshotters too? I see a scheduled snapshot that coincided with coldstarts in the timeline.

sasha: paused noncritical snapshots for 20m: `snapshotter pause --region ap-southeast1 --tag noncritical --dur 1200s`. ops-bot: "snapshot pause accepted"

janitor-bot: "set-concurrency --pool ap-se1-poolC --concurrency 1 executed"

omar: monitoring queries we should watch: `avg(nvme_avg_queue_size{cohort="ap-se1-poolC"})`, `rate(gpu_attach_errors[1m])`, `sum(rate(nvme_io_time_seconds_total[1m])) by (cohort)`.

sasha: rolled attach timeout canary at 02:09 UTC. after backoff, attach success normalized by 02:12 UTC. leaving backoff for 20m to be safe.

chen: follow-ups: 1) add scheduler hysteresis so 429s don't result in simultaneous flood when limit resets, 2) add coldstart-aware scrub-window avoidance (tagging), 3) investigate NVMe firmware and thermal sensors on hosts that saw highest avgqu. I saw one with a thermal throttle spike at 02:06 in the host log.

omar: also request a quick audit of kernel options for write coalescing; maybe tune commit interval for coldstart windows (short-term). but be careful — don't mask data integrity issues.

sasha: cost note: fallback/dedicated fallback during the ~4m window estimated +$950. logging to incident-costs.

rachel: filing tickets: INFRA-2154 (scheduler hysteresis), INFRA-2155 (coldstart scrub avoidance), INFRA-2156 (host thermal + fw audit).

sasha: will keep cordons off but we flagged 3 hosts for follow-up; if reoccurs we'll cordon and drain. closing loop unless it reappears. :white_check_mark:
